## ✨ Added

- **Per-domain Healthchecks URLs.** Under Settings → Notifications, next to the global Healthchecks URL, you can now set a separate check URL for containers, VMs, flash and the app config. A domain with its own URL pings its own check (its own start / success / failure, its own runtime and history), so you can see exactly which domain ran, when, and how long it took, instead of everything landing on one shared check. Leave a domain's field blank and it falls back to the global URL, so nothing changes unless you opt in. The Test button now checks every distinct URL you've configured. (#27, thanks @ptmorris1)

## Fixed

- **Scheduled restore drills no longer silently fail or read wrong on the dashboard.** (#30, thanks @manilx) Several things were compounding:
  - The scheduled drill shared a per-domain lock with scheduled off-site replication/backup, and grabbed it non-blocking - so when they fired together it silently gave up recording nothing, leaving the dashboard stuck on "never" while a manual run minutes later succeeded. The scheduled drill now waits for the domain to be free (up to a bounded window) and always records a result; a manual drill still returns immediately if the domain is busy.
  - The drill didn't clear a stale restic lock before its check/restore step (the same class of stale-lock bug fixed for tagging in v4.4.1), so a leftover off-site lock could make it fail. It now self-heals a stale lock first.
  - The ransomware scorecard's "restore drill" row read green purely from how recent the last drill was, even if that drill had **failed** - contradicting the red "proven restorable from off-site" pill. The row (and the overall posture chip) now honor the actual pass/fail outcome.
  - Running a drill from Settings now refreshes the dashboard so the result shows without a manual reload.
- **The flash backup no longer includes a `.git` folder.** (#31, thanks @BaukeZwart) If your Unraid flash has a `.git` (from a plugin or a manual git-tracking of `/boot`), BombVault used to back it up while Unraid's own flash backup skips it. It's now excluded from the flash backup, matching Unraid and keeping the backups a little smaller. (A stray `.git` never actually broke the USB creator, but parity is nicer.)

- **Off-site repositories on backends like Jottacloud now initialize.** BombVault bundled rclone from Debian's package (v1.60.1), which is too old for some backends - Jottacloud in particular returned an HTTP 500 `AllocationException` when restic tried to create the repo's key, so it never wrote `config` and the repository looked non-existent. BombVault now bundles the current official rclone binary (v1.74.x), the same way it already pulls the current restic instead of Debian's stale one. If you hit this on Jottacloud (or any other backend that needs a newer rclone), pull the new image and retry. (#32, thanks @strese)

---

- **A backup no longer starts a "stop during backup" dependency that was already stopped.** (#33, thanks @ptmorris1) The container you back up already followed detect-state (a stopped one stays stopped), but the *other* containers you configure to stop for the duration of a backup (e.g. a database an app depends on) were being restarted unconditionally afterward. Because stopping an already-stopped container is a no-op success at the Docker daemon, an already-off dependency landed in the "restart these" list and got started. In a backup-all of an app plus its stopped database it could even cascade (the database gets started, then its own backup sees it running and restarts it too). Dependencies now follow the same detect-state rule as the main container: only the ones that were actually running before the backup are stopped and restarted.
- **Config backups can now be deleted.** (#34, thanks @ptmorris1) The Config page listed its self-backup snapshots but had no way to remove one - the delete engine already supported the config domain, it just wasn't exposed. Each config snapshot now has a delete button, matching the flash and container pages. Off-site append-only repositories still refuse deletes (the refusal is surfaced as an error, as elsewhere).

---

- **BombVault no longer leaves behind zombie (`<defunct>`) `rclone` processes.** (#35, thanks @strese) BombVault runs as PID 1 inside its container and shells out to restic, which forks its own `rclone` helper for off-site/cloud repos. When a backup or check is cancelled or times out (the off-site check timeout, a manual cancel, a WAN drop, a container restart), restic gets killed and its rclone helper is left orphaned onto PID 1. A plain Go binary running as PID 1 does not reap adopted processes, so those orphans piled up as `[rclone] <defunct>` over time. The image now runs `tini` as its init (PID 1), which reaps orphaned subprocesses automatically (this also covers the analogous virsh-over-ssh orphans from VM backups). It is baked into the image, so there is nothing to configure. As a bonus, `docker stop` is now faster: the container shuts down cleanly instead of waiting out the stop grace period.

To pick up the fix, pull the updated image and recreate the container.

---

## Changed

- The **ransomware protection card** on the dashboard is now shown only in **Advanced** view.
- The **Advanced** sidebar row is now a checkbox and matches the font of the other sidebar rows.
